en: Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Venerable Tánfāng.
In the second year of the Zhìzhèng era, the Venerable Tánfāng Zhōng traveled from Mount Zhōng to Mount Jiān.

Monks from all quarters flocked to follow him in great numbers. Those who gained insight from what they heard spoke of it to one another, and these accounts were transmitted throughout the four directions. Its...
Tu Zhengmou went into the mountains of Linchuan and informed me of the various Buddhist activities there. Upon hearing this, I sighed and said:
"One who preaches the Dharma should preach it according to the Dharma; it is at Jing Mountain that this is truly found. For this reason, I inscribed these words at its beginning.

Three years later, by imperial decree, I came to reside at the Great Longxiang Temple to propagate the winds of our school, where both monastics and laypeople held me in profound reverence. At that time—

His disciples, including Zhuzhiquan and Jizuzu, further compiled the recorded sayings he delivered at Chongyin, Jiangshan Chongxi, Jing Mountain Longxiang, and [the fifth location], binding them into a single volume titled the *Wuhui Lu* (Record of the Five Assemblies). Four of these assemblies took place in Jiankang.
One of these is located in Hangzhou; both are supreme and unsurpassed.

Just as it would be rare for a person from Laṅkā to ascend even one of them, so too, wherever this Master goes, his preaching of the Dharma flows forth abundantly—who could possibly surpass him? His disciple Shirei has come to request that I provide a preface for him.
I have heard that in the past, the worthy ones such as Prime Minister Pei [Hui] set forth the essential heart of Huangbo, and Su Dongpo, the Gatekeeper of Literature, opened...
The lofty style of Zhenjing established the essential tenets of his school; he was not one who indulged in empty words. How could I possibly express this?
Having observed the arrival of Bodhidharma, the lineage of the Linji school has had a far-reaching and grand beginning. During the Southern Song dynasty...
The disciples of Yuanwu were Long and Gao, both of whom deeply served the True Lineage and strove earnestly to succeed to the Dharma.
Long was dignified and solemn, profound and silent without a trace; Gao was grand and resolute, like the breaking forth of the Yangtze and Yellow Rivers.
While Gao stayed at Yangyu for less than a single summer, thirteen people attained enlightenment under him—an unprecedented occurrence in recent times.
Yet the true lineage of Yangqi was transmitted by Yuanwu Keqin to Ying’an Hua, a senior disciple of Dahui Zonggao.

Zonggao possessed the public spirit of non-self, while Dahui possessed the reality of having found a worthy successor; therefore, those who emerged from Zonggao have branched out in thousands of stems and ten thousand leaves.
That each ray of light corresponded to the realization of the two masters at Yun’an was truly a most pitiable and wondrous sight.
Huade received Mian Shanjie; as Shanjie was about to pass away, he brooded for a long time. His attendant stepped forward and said, "Does the Master have some thoughts?
He replied, "It is not for you to know. The attendant continued, "I have been staying here at Mount Yue for a long time. Startled and delighted, [Shanjie] summoned Yue.
Upon seeing [the robe] once, he donned it and entered nirvana. This illustrates how this school does not seek to merely acquire disciples;
such was the case here. He belonged to the lineage of Songyuan. Yue obtained the "Non-obtainment," from which Tong obtained it; Tong transmitted it to Xuzhou Du, and Du transmitted it to Yushan Zhen.
Now, I, Tanfang, am a disciple of Zhen. As for the mind-to-mind transmission, the school possesses no separate dharma;
as one preaches the dharma in accordance with the dharma, the dharma possesses no fixed words. By means of words one contemplates the dharma, and by means of the dharma one seeks the source.

Yet when tracing back the mind-to-mind transmission through the *yulu* (recorded sayings), it ultimately depends upon the person. Alas! Though it is said that "no reliance is placed on words and letters,"
This is the fundamental principle. Now, as vast as mountains and seas, it cannot be described in terms of existence or non-existence; it already lies beyond words.
I shall briefly set forth these humble remarks to serve as a prologue.
Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Venerable Tánfāng, by the Layman Wéixiào of Shǔ Commandery,
Yú Jí, on the day after the full moon in the tenth month of winter in the sixth year of Zhìzhèng, the Bingxū year.

The Recorded Sayings of Venerable Tánfāng of Chóngyīn Chan Monastery, Jiankang Road.
Compiled by Jìzǔ and others, the Dharma Heirs who served as the Abbot of Shànquán Chan Monastery, Changzhou Road.
On the first day of the third month in the ninth year of the Dàdé era, the year of Yǐsĩ (1305), the Master accepted his invitation at the Head Seat’s Quarters and pointed [to the assembly].
The Dharma Seat Master said: "The entire earth is this precious Sumeru throne;
what levels or grades could there be? He gave a shout: "Blue sky and sun, a thunderbolt crashes! Then he ascended the seat and offered incense, saying:
"This incense is specifically for the long life of the Great Yuan Sovereign, the current Emperor. Ten thousand years! Ten thousand years! Ten thousand ten thousand years! We humbly pray that he..."
The Sage’s brilliance is like the sun and the moon; I pray that Your Majesty’s sagely years may endure as long as earth and heaven. Next, he held up the incense and said:

"This single portion of incense, burned within the burner, is offered to供养 (venerate) my late teacher, the Great Master Yushan, the Chan Master Foguang Haiyin, who formerly resided at Jingde Lingyuan Chan Temple in Hangzhou Prefecture, in order to repay the kindness of his Dharma-milk. He then sat cross-legged upon the seat.
The question and answer concluded. He then said: "The past is already past; the future is yet to come.
As for this great matter of Śākyamuni’s life and legacy, it is now fully entrusted to Xin-chong. He then opened both hands and said:
"If you all can believe this, the imperial grace and the Buddha’s grace will be repaid at once. Should your emotional defilements not yet be exhausted, or if you still cling to the Dharma..."

"Not yet forgotten. A phoenix entwined in a golden net hastens toward the Milky Way with no fixed time; a serpent deity guards its pearl, harboring wind and thunder while remaining in self-obscuration.
After a long pause: "It is easier to transform cinder into gold and jade than it is to exhort people to eliminate right and wrong.
He spoke again: "Just now, Master Jiangshan struck the gavel and said: 'O assembly of dragons and elephants at this Dharma feast, you should contemplate the primary principle.'"
Furthermore, how can one proclaim the primary meaning? *Tut!* Do not take it all as the view of a wild fox.
Entering the hall [he said]: "The entire earth is this gate of liberation; why cannot you enter it?
The entire earth is this Jewel Flower King’s throne; why cannot you sit upon it? The green creeper winds its way up to the very summit of the cold pine. White...
The clouds are limpid and vast, appearing and disappearing within the great void. Entering the hall, he said:
"A single rain universally nourishes the three types of grass and two kinds of trees; the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye is beyond the sands of Ganges.
The Golden-Colored Dhūta descends from Mount Kukkutapāda. He struck his whisk and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following story: Shitou uttered a *chuyǔ* (a vertical statement), saying, "Words and active functions have no connection [to the truth].
Yaoshan stepped forward from the assembly and said, "Even to attain that which is beyond words and active functions still has no connection.

Shitou said, "In my place here, not even a needle can pierce through. Yaoshan said, "In my place here, it is like planting flowers upon a rock. The Master said, "The pearl is within the formless mind of the *wangxiang*."
The palm. Where Li Lou walks, the waves overflow the heavens.
Meeting the Five, he addresses the assembly: throughout the twelve hours of the day, do not rely on a single thing. A black ox lies dead in the water;
descending from heaven, surging up from the earth—under his heels, thirty blows are well-deserved. I respectfully address those who investigate the profound: do not let your time pass in vain.
Wasted in vain.
On the occasion of the Buddha’s Birthday, he ascended the hall and raised the topic:

"When the Elder Śākyamuni was first born, he walked seven steps, looked around in the four directions, pointed to heaven and earth, and said, 'In the heavens above and the earth below, I alone am honored. At that time, I..."
"If you see [him], strike him dead with a single blow and feed him to the dogs; this is for the sake of bringing peace to the world. The Master remarked:
"Having once been at the place where the monkeys cry out over the Gorges of Ba, even hearing a donkey bray would break one's heart."
The Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat. Looking over the assembly, he said:
"All of you have traveled thousands of miles, abandoning your teachers, parents, and kin, to come here seeking Buddhas and Patriarchs.

Do you not know that Bodhidharma was a mere old barbarian, Śākyamuni was a dry piece of dung, Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra were dung-carriers, and the two stages of Equal and Wondrous Enlightenment are..."
To shatter the attachments of ordinary people: Bodhi and Nirvana are tethering stakes for donkeys; the twelve divisions of the teachings are registers of ghosts and spirits;
the four fruits and three stages of worthiness are mere paper for wiping sores. From the first thought-moment to the ten stages, these are ghosts guarding ancient tombs, unable to save themselves.
[The Master] suddenly brandishes his staff and says, "Deshan is coming! Then he sets down the staff: "Abiding in the world as if in empty space."
"Just as a lotus flower is not stained by water, the purity of mind transcends even that.
[The Master] ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas appeared in the world; the Patriarchs came from the West—this was already an 'unattached' matter.

Yet they gather in groups of three hundred or five hundred, speaking of yellow and describing black, pointing east and drawing west; these are merely the views of wild foxes. He raised his staff and said: "Observe!"
World-Honored Avalokiteśvara buys sesame cakes with money; when he lets go of his hand, they turn out to be steamed buns. [The Master] leans on his staff and descends from the seat.
Entering the hall for formal discourse, he cites a monk who asked Zhaozhou, “What is the crown-mark of Vairocana? Zhaozhou replied, “I have been a monk since childhood.”
It was never a case of visual distortion. Suppose someone were to suddenly ask Qing Shan, "What is the crown-mark (uṣṇīṣa) of Vairocana? He would simply reply to him:
"The snow is spun into silk, and the mulberry trees turn green again; the yellow clouds of grain are harvested, and the rice is now a true green.
Now tell me, is this the same as Zhaozhou’s [answer], or is it different?
When the Head Seat Liaotang of Yangshan arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "The Mahāyāna Dharma transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations.
At Chongyin Temple, the drum is beaten for the assembly to ascend the hall; team after team of monks comes, team after team of monks goes. *He shouted.*
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked Touzi, "Is there still the dragon’s cry within the withered tree?
Touzi replied, "I say that within your skull, the lion roars. The Master offered this verse: The old dragon cries in the withered tree;
The lion roars within the skull. Nine times nine is eighty-one: Facing south, one looks toward the Big Dipper.
The Small General Talk for the End of the Summer Retreat: In all other quarters there are phrases for saving people; at Green Mountain there are no phrases for saving people.

In all other quarters there are the "sword that kills" and the "sword that gives life"; at Green Mountain there is neither the sword that kills nor the sword that gives life. In all other quarters there is binding and there is releasing.
The green mountains have neither knot nor release. You people here are standing right in this place—do you still have blood under your skin?
If I, this mountain monk, were to look at it, the Buddhas of the three periods would not equal you; the patriarchs of the six generations would not equal you;
the old monks of the world would not equal you. He further said: "There is no need for deliberation, and no need for doubt. Look!
The preceding teaching is the total presentation of the Dharma. "Right now, rest and simply rest; if you seek the moment of realization, there is no such moment.
[He stood for a long time. "珍重" (Chen zhong—take care). He ascended the hall and said:
"Light and darkness come and go, but empty space has no movement or turning. Since the myriad phenomena are clearly manifest, the One Truth is of itself..."
[The Master] looked in the mirror. He held up his whisk and said, "Śākyamuni Buddha is upon the tip of this whisk, preaching the essential Dharma.
He lowered the whisk and said, "Seeing that you all do not understand, he has run away into the pillar. He gave a shout and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "An ancient worthy said: 'At Wuhu one sees Wuhu; at Dangtu one sees Dangtu.
On the night of the fifteenth day of the eighth month, it is just like a handleless fan. Beautiful indeed, but it is not quite right.
Qingshan is not so: with eyes open, one sees; with eyes closed, one sees. Wuhu and Dangtu do not go beyond the Hall of the Cold Palace. [He] gave a shout.
"Ha! He descends from his seat.
Entering the hall, the Fifth Patriarch said: "The Patriarchs could not describe it; the Buddha-eye cannot see it. It is the grandmotherly heart [of compassion] on all four sides."
"I shall open a single thread for you, my lord. On the path of the green mountains: as soon as one opens the mouth, it is spoken; as soon as one opens the eyes, it is seen.
The old woman of the green mountains—when has she ever opened a single thread? He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "The teachings state: 'When one person gives rise to the true and returns to the source, the voids of the ten directions all vanish away.
The Buddha Hall brushes against your nostrils; the bell tower stuffs your skull. How can you achieve resonance with this?"
*Ha!* [He] ascended the hall and said:
"If you wish to understand the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should contemplate the conditions of time and season. When the time and season arrive, its principle manifests of itself.
The sound of the bell at night in stillness is never deficient regardless of how it is struck; the moon’s reflection in a clear pool is not disturbed by the ripples of the waves."
Scattered. It is so, yet it is also not so. It is both so and not so—altogether permissible. (He strikes the whisk.
A lion does not eat the leftovers of a vulture; a swift falcon does not kill a dead hare. Descent from the seat.
Winter Solstice Small Lecture. Old Śākyamuni has no sinews in his eyes; Great Master Bodhidharma has no blood beneath his skin.

You all know only to count the nine days from the winter solstice and the three white days before the end of the year, yet you do not know that last night an old plum branch, facing south, was snapped by the frost.
(He strikes the meditation seat once with his whisk. Again he says: Before the Peak of Shaoshi, the gold...
The phoenix dances; on the path of Caoxi, the jade rooster crows. On this night of green mountains, the evening drum for the assembly is struck.

To spare a moment for the idle monk to stand, I invite the Abbot of Xizhou to ascend the hall. Rolling up and unfolding, he establishes the heaven and earth beyond the square; traversing and intersecting, he hangs the sun and moon across the realm.
The Moon. The Head Seat strikes the board for seated meditation; the Elder proclaims the essential tenets of the school; Hanshan and Shide sweep the floor and prepare the incense;
Maitreya and Śākyamuni carry firewood and draw water. Then, he descends from his seat.
Ascending the Dharma Hall for the Lantern Festival to address the two orders of officials: The Buddhas emit radiance to assist in the realization of the meaning of the True Mark (*dharmatā*).

On the east side are the administrators (*karmadāna*); on the west side are the heads of departments (*sthavira*). Herein the banner of the Dharma is erected; herein the administrative regulations are established.
A thousand lamps continue the flame; tigers gallop and dragons soar. One flower and five petals endure as long as earth and heaven. (With the whisk, he strikes the meditation seat.)
Descending from the seat. Ascending the hall: The spring breeze fans day and night; the spring rain nourishes in due season. Since the people of Caoxi do not come, my thoughts drift idly toward them.
(He strikes the meditation platform. Descending from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The fundamental nature is pure and still; how is it that mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise?
All you practitioners of Chan: the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are your own selves; your own selves are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth.

Pure and still by nature, they pervade all things. He patted the meditation seat and said: "From the Buddha Hall one runs out through the mountain gate; from the Sangha Hall one passes straight through the kitchen."
[The Master] struck the gavel once.
He ascended the hall and said: "Mind is Buddha; neither mind nor Buddha. It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not an object.
Peach and plum blossoms bloom amidst the fire; at twilight, one awaits the rising sun."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "An ancient worthy said: 'If for a single thought-moment your mind harbors doubt, you are obstructed by earth; if for a single thought-moment your mind is deluded, you are drowned by water;
if for a single thought-moment your mind is angry, you are burned by fire; if for a single thought-moment your mind is joyful, you are blown away by wind. He then held up his whisk and said:
'Earth, water, fire, and wind are right now upon the tip of this whisk, preaching the Dharma and listening to the Dharma. He struck the whisk."
"Two arise from one; even that one must not be clung to. When the single mind does not arise, the myriad dharmas are without fault.
[The Master] ascended the hall and raised the example: One day Yunmen said, "In the capital, are there still any pillars and beams?

He then provided his own response on behalf of the questioner: "Every household has Avalokiteśvara. [The Master] commented: "Master Yunmen was much like one who suppresses the noble to make them lowly. Now tell me: the green mountains..."
There were also no ridgepoles or beams. The Head of the Hall said: "In every monastery, lanterns burn like broad daylight;
beneath the incense burner, one sits playing the sheng flute.
Changqieduo painted Buddhist images. The Master spoke a verse to show him: "From the tip of the brush, he conjures forth various Buddha-images; these are said to be..."
Is it the mind? Is it the hand? When both mind and hand are forgotten, one knows where [the truth] falls. The spring colors of Shaolin reach to the ends of the earth.

Compiled by Dharma-heirs Jizu and others, this is the *Recorded Sayings* of Venerable Tanyang at Taiping Xingguo Chan Temple on Mount Jiangshan in Jiankang Road, and at Shanguan Chan Temple in Changzhou Road.

In the first year of the Zhizhi era, the year of Xinyou, on the seventeenth day of the first month, the Master accepted the formal invitation from the Xuanzheng Yuan to enter the temple and take possession of his quarters.
Holding his staff horizontally across him, he said, "If you aim, you invite the arrow; if you do not aim, there are one hundred and eight thousand [paths].
He leaned the staff against himself and said, "I let this one move pass. Thereupon he emerged and ascended the seat. Having offered incense and finished his prayers for the Emperor, he sat.
Having finished the exchange of questions and answers while seated, he said: "Practice the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma; the banner of the Dharma is established wherever it may be.

Today, at the new Jiangshan, the hall is opened. Through one question and one answer, one pressing and one probing, we adapt to the exigencies of the times to assist in propagating the sacred transformation."
If you say that this is "establishing the banner of the Dharma," you will enter hell like a shot arrow.
Do you not see how Linji said to Puhua, "I wish to establish the fundamental tenets of Huangbo; you must thoroughly assist me in doing so"?
Puhua said, "Take care," and immediately went down the steps. Later, Ke Fu arrived, and Linji questioned him in the same way; Ke Fu also said, "Take care," and went down the steps.
Three days later, Puhua went up to inquire after him, saying, "What did you say the day before yesterday, Master? Linji raised his staff and struck him down.
Again, three days later, Puhua went up to inquire after him, saying, "Master, why did you strike Puhua the day before yesterday?"
"What business is there? Ji picked up his staff and struck him down as well. The Master gave a shout and said:

"If one lacked such an eye for selecting the Buddha, how could the wind of the patriarchal school have reached the present day? He then raised another case: One day the World-Honored One ascended the seat;

Kāśyapa struck the gavel and said, "The World-Honored One has finished preaching the Dharma," whereupon the World-Honored One descended from the seat. The Master said: "The dragon’s sleeve is swept aside."
The whole body is manifested. Where the Elephant King walks, the tracks of foxes are severed.
[Ascending the hall: "The myriad dharmas are the light of the mind; all conditions are nothing but the clarity of nature. Originally there is no person who is deluded or awakened;
it simply requires realization today. But tell me, what is it that is realized? If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata’s true Dharma."
The Wheel of Dharma.
Advancing and retreating, both classes ascend the hall. Amidst the conditions of suffering and joy, adversity and favor, all Buddhas are born.

Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra, the Teachers, employ inverse practices to transform through compliance. How magnificent are these men of noble virtue! They support the broken-legged cauldron, boiling rice and boiling again.
The soup is served; at both meals, nothing is lacking. If a mustard seed were to fall to the ground, the void would shatter into dust.

[He] strikes the whisk and descends from the seat. Entering the hall: A thousand peaks stand in emerald array, ten thousand ravines vie for beauty. Orioles sing at the valley mouth; swallows chatter within the rafters. Vairocana...
The Mind-Seal is vast and boundless; the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye circulates without interruption. [The Master] raises his staff: "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva buys a sesame cake with money;
when he lets go of his hand, it turns out to be a steamed bun. [He] strikes the ground with the staff: "When there is spirit, one adds even more spirit;
where there is no elegance, there is elegance nonetheless."

A Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat: The teachings of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the canon—whether expounded horizontally or vertically—and the direct or indirect expositions of the elder monks throughout the land, all amount to nothing more than trying to cure a dead horse with medicine.
You, the assembly gathered here, occupy the Bodhisattva Vehicle and cultivate the practice of quiescent extinction.
With Great Perfect Enlightenment as your monastery, you dwell in peace within body and mind, abiding in the Wisdom of Equal Nature. [The text continues: three lives, six...
Ten kalpas. Ultimately, how is it? "The moonlight of a single day shines without ceasing; the pine winds from ten thousand ravines shake the courtyard gates.

Again, he raised the case: Linji addressed the assembly, saying, "Upon this lump of red flesh, there is a true person of no station who constantly enters and exits through the gate of the face of all of you.
Those who have not yet attained verification, look! A monk stepped forward and asked, "What is..."
Linji seized the person of no-position as he descended from his meditation seat and said, "What kind of dried dung pellet is this 'person of no-position'?
The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "All you practitioners of Chan, those who have not yet attained realization must most certainly avoid being careless.
Linji said, 'What kind of dried dung pellet is this "person of no-position"? Do you understand? The fish has already leaped away with the flowing current; the oriole still..."
Returning with fallen blossoms.
Upon the conclusion of the assembly for viewing the Tripitaka at court, he ascended the hall and said:

"From the Deer Park at the beginning to the Bahudhika River at the end—within these two intervals, not a single word was ever spoken. Some might then say: "The jade rollers and lapis lazuli cases contain five thousand scrolls of scripture."
"Ye, from where have you come? Truly, I say that the wisdom I have attained is subtle and supreme.
Sentient beings have dull faculties; they are attached to pleasure and blinded by doubt. For such as these, how can they be delivered? [He then brandished his staff.]
Gautama has arrived! He raises the sun and moon in the realm of awakening and spreads the voice of compassion throughout the sands of worlds.
At times he manifests great supernormal powers, and at times he emits great radiance; he rescues sentient beings and delivers them from the sea of suffering. How majestic! How vast!
There is no contrivance; there is no partiality. With this, I offer prayers for the Sage’s longevity, that his phoenix calendar may enjoy eternal spring.
With this, I assist the imperial design, that it may endure as long as heaven. Even so, this is still not yet the matter of the ultimate limit.
But tell me, what is the matter of the ultimate limit? He plants his staff in the ground and says: "The rustic elder knows nothing of the labors of Yao and Shun; drum, drum, beat the drum!"

Offering to the River Spirit. Again, it is recounted: The King of the Kingdom of Eastern India, while observing the monks as they were reading the sutras, noticed that the Venerable Prajñātāra sat in silence.
The King asked, "While the assembly of monks is reading the sutras, why does the Venerable One not read the sutras?"
The Venerable One said: "With the exhalation, one does not involve oneself in myriad conditions; with the inhalation, one does not dwell within the realms of the aggregates.

He constantly turns such a sutra hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of times. The Master commented: "The King of Eastern India and the Venerable One engaged in a question-and-answer session, knowing only the first [part] but not the second.
Today at Jiangshan, the Imperial Court has bestowed the Imperial Incense upon this patch-robed monk."

There were over one hundred and seventy members of the household and five thousand forty-eight fascicles of the Sūtras, Vinaya, and Abhidharma. Within seven days, he recited them from beginning to end;
this truly served to accord with the Will of Heaven above and provide sustenance for the common people below, thereby being worthy of repaying the unrepayable debt of gratitude.
Together we assist in the unconditioned transformation.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The source of returning to the origin is non-dual; the gates of expedient means are manifold. The wildcat and the white ox are driven forth;
the iron ox of Shanzhou tramples the Great Image of Jiazhou. He struck his whisk and said: "Rewards are given to those who have merit."
The Head Seat Xie held the whisk and the Abbot Bianzhai presided over the meal; they ascended the hall.
That phrase which the Buddhas of the three periods, the patriarchs of the six generations, and the old monks of the world have never been able to express—its hundred flavors are now complete.
Today, our Head Seat and Abbot have brought it all forth at once, so that every single person who sees or hears it shall depart with a deep, contented sigh of fullness. And so it is!
The Way. Does this mountain monk still remain within it? (He strikes the meditation staff. "A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool. He ascends the hall.
"If you see it as a pillar, you do not see the pillar; if you do not see it as a pillar, you do not see the pillar. Right and wrong have already departed; [it exists] within right and wrong."
I recommend this for you all. All you virtuous practitioners of Chan: Śākyamuni Buddha has been turning the Great Dharma Wheel amidst right and wrong without ceasing;
countless sentient beings have attained equal and perfect enlightenment amidst right and wrong without ceasing.
(He strikes the whisk and descends from his seat.)

Ascending the hall, he said: "The Perfect is identical to the great void; there is neither deficiency nor excess. Amidst the blazing heat of midsummer, flakes of ice fly about. He then took up his whisk and said:
"Śākyamuni Buddha, right now upon the tip of this mountain monk’s whisk, enters samādhi in the east and arises in the west;
enters samādhi in the west and arises in the east; enters samādhi in the south and arises in the north; enters samādhi in the north..."
He enters meditative absorption in the south and arises in the north; he enters absorption above and arises below; he enters absorption below and arises above.
He brandishes his whisk and says: "Quickly fix your eyes upon it!"
The Small General Instruction for the End of the Summer Retreat: "The Buddhas did not appear in the world; the Patriarchs did not come from the West.

Within the sphere of every person, it is like a thousand suns shining together, pervading and penetrating the ten directions of empty space. During these ninety days of this summer retreat, how could I, this mountain monk, allow you all to err by even a single hair’s breadth?
Yaoshan had not ascended the hall for a long time. The head of the monastery said, 'The assembly has long been longing for the Master’s instruction.'"

The Master said, "Strike the bell. When the assembly had gathered, Yaoshan returned to his quarters. The head of the monastery said, "Earlier this morning, you granted the assembly permission for the Master to preach the Dharma;
why then did you not utter a single word? Yaoshan replied, "The sutras have their own masters, and the treatises have their own masters.
How can one blame me for that? Does the great assembly understand? It is like being accustomed to passing through the Five-Phoenix Pavilion."
"Pass it here. Holding a golden whip in his hand, he celebrates the Great Peace. Again, [the Master] raised this case:

One phrase: a fierce tiger grows wings. One phrase: a dragon obtains clouds and rain.
One phrase: there is no handle at all. One phrase: not worth a single coin. If you can discern each of these, I grant you leave from your studies.
If you simply say for all of them, "Ten thousand miles of white clouds," do not slander this mountain monk. Descend from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "A sandalwood grove is surrounded by sandalwood; a thornbush grove is surrounded by thorns.
Sometimes a sandalwood grove is surrounded by thorns; sometimes a thornbush grove is surrounded by sandalwood.
As you all enter and exit within them, do you possess any freedom? [He] struck once with the staff and said: 'The water falls, and the rocks appear.'"
His head emerges. Deep in the forest, the grasses and trees are fragrant.
He ascends the hall. His trousers have no crotch; his breeches have no opening. On his head are three or five pecks of green ash.
What need is there to speak of the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics? Then he descends from the seat.
Small-scale Sermon for the End of the Summer Retreat: I observe that the Tathāgata does not depart from the past, does not come from the future, and likewise has no dwelling in the present.
O virtuous practitioners of meditation, where have you established yourselves and sustained your lives during these ninety days?

If you can understand this, then Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva spent the summer retreat in three places while the brilliant sun shone across the heavens; Yangshan tilled a patch of fallow land and sowed a basket of grain. [He] cut it down.
It is like cutting through iron with a chisel. If you do not know this, you will sit upon an iron bed and swallow hot iron; do not say I did not warn you.

Upon the conclusion of the retreat, I ascend the hall: for ninety days we observed the *jinzu* (foot-binding) period, and now that the sacred regulation is fulfilled, we remain as we were before in Pūrvavideha.
Regarding the directions: West Jambudvīpa remains as West Jambudvīpa; South Jambudvīpa remains as South Jambudvīpa;
North Uttarakuru remains as North Uttarakuru. Striking the meditation seat with the whisk, he said:
"Day and night it radiates light, illuminating existence and non-existence; yet the deluded call this the *pāramitās*."

On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall and raised the following case: When Master Mazu was enjoying the moon with Nanyuan, Xitang, and Baizhang, Mazu asked, "At this very moment, what is it?
Baizhang said, "It is precisely the time for cultivation. Xitang said, "It is precisely the time for making offerings.
Nanyuan shook his sleeves and walked away. Mazu remarked, "The Sutras return to the Tripitaka; Zen returns to the sea. Only Puyan alone transcends all things."
Wai. The Master’s verse says: Father and son follow one another into the Broad Cold; Toying with shadows and light is truly groundless.
How much better it would be to see things as they are in common experience: The Milky Way is silent as the Jade Plate revolves.
I request that the two elders, Zhongdaxi Yuan and Cuwei Xingtian, be appointed as the Head Seat (Shouzuo) of the Front and Rear Halls.
Ascending the hall, he took up the "axe for tending the mountain" and said: "The wind and moon of Longhe are shared equally;
fifteen hundred followers follow my lofty steps. The numinous light behind the elbow shines upon the crown of the head. He then cited a case: A monk asked Cuwei, "What is..."
Regarding the Great Meaning of the Buddha-Dharma, Xuefeng said, "Hand me the meditation board. When the monk handed him the board, Xuefeng took it and struck him.
He then asked Linji, "What is the Great Meaning of the Buddha-Dharma? Linji replied, "Hand me the meditation cushion."
The monk stepped onto the meditation cushion. Linji caught him and struck him immediately. The Master commented:

"O assembly, when this monk asked in such a manner, and the two great elders, Cuiwei and Linji, answered in such a manner—was it that illumination and function were simultaneous, or was there some other superior quality?
[He] suddenly took up his staff and struck twice. 'If one lacks such an eye for the selection of Buddhas, how could the winds of the school ever reach here?'"

Now, ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: A monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall? Yunmen said, "The golden wind reveals its essence. The Master composed a verse:
When the trees wither and the leaves fall, he asks Yunmen; Within a smile, he turns the heavens and revolves the earth. In the blazing summer heat...
The clouds return to the azure caverns; in the clear autumn, jade dew drips into the golden basin.
Entering the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: When Fenggan traveled to Mount Wutai, he asked Hanshan and Shide, "If you go with me to travel Mount Wutai, you are of my same kind.
If you do not go with me to travel Mount Wutai, you are not of my same kind. Hanshan—
Hanshan asked, "Where are you going? Fenggan replied, "To pay homage to Mañjuśrī. Hanshan said, "You are not of my kind. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented:
"Although Hanshan, Shide, and Fenggan were not of the same kind, there was something similar among them.
Do you understand, monks? The fading clouds fly alongside the solitary wild goose; the autumn waters merge with the vast expanse of heaven."
Form. Descend from your seat.
Entering the hall: a north wind blows the sand, withered branches cry out in the cold. At Shaolin, he faced the wall for nine years, starving and freezing;
his legacy even reached Changqing, who sat until seven grass cushions were worn through, yet claimed he attained realization at the moment the curtain was rolled back. Ho! Ho!
Ascending the hall, he said: "The teachings state: 'All that has form is entirely illusory. If one sees that all forms are no-form, then one sees the Tathāgata.
Are the monks and laypeople present here illusory? Are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth illusory? Are the sun, moon, and stars illusory?
Is even the statement that 'all forms are no-form' illusory? If so, where is the Old Man Śākyamuni?"
He strikes the meditation bench with his whisk and descends from the seat.
Upon returning from his retreat, he ascends the hall and says: "Today I recall coming here last year; last year I was certain to depart this very morning. He takes up his staff and says:
"The knotted staff slung across the shoulder, heedless of others, he strides straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand crags to dwell there."
On the first day of the third month in the year of Jizheng Bingxu, the Master retired to Longpan Hermitage awaiting imperial summons.

On the thirteenth day of the seventh month, the monastery was destroyed by fire. The Grand Councilor of the Provincial Administration, Duke Nalin Gao, led his subordinates to invite the Master to reside there once more;
he entered the monastery on the fifteenth day to take up his duties. In the spring of the following year, the temple was completed, and he ascended the hall [to preach]. (Recorded by Jin)

The lands and dragons soar upward into the heavens; from Yāma and Tuṣita, they ride upon clouds to arrive. Though the axes and hoes remain unmoved, as if everything were as it was before, the multi-storied pavilions open one after another in succession.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked Yunmen, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still any transgression?
Yunmen said, "Mount Sumeru. The Master offered this verse: "How laughable is the old, ancient sage Yunmen! From his mouth he suddenly brings forth five Mount Sumers.
The worlds of the ten directions are now pure and peaceful; To whom else could he further explain the fundamental principles?"
The Great Hall enshrines the Buddhas of the Three Ages; the rite of opening the light is performed.
When the Imperial Yuan dynasty first established the Palace of the Dharma King, the Tathāgatas of the three ages manifested their great merit. In an instant, they have returned to Tuṣita Heaven;
yet when one lifts the eyes, the palaces appear again in endless layers. O Assembly! Today, the sacred image of the Greatly Awakened World-Honored One has its light opened.
"Clear! Now tell me: is there light that can be opened? Or is there no light that can be opened? If you say there is, the Buddha-body is unconditioned and does not fall into any categories.
If you say there is not, then even drawing a Buddha image with one's fingernails yields immeasurable and supreme merit.
If you attain clarity here, the true Buddha appears before you. If this is still not the case, you must further bring it forth. He then made a dot with his brush.
Yanshi said: "The ninety-seven marks of a great man—A single path of divine light amidst ten thousand tranquil realms.
When the Crown Prince was staying at the palace of Liang Wang, he once visited Jiangshan Mountain and, during a conversation with the Master, asked:
"What is meant by 'Jiangbo porridge'? The Master replied: "I thought Your Highness had forgotten. He asked again: "What is meant by 'the patched-robed monk'?"
"What are these three socks at home? He replied, "I have traversed every mountain and river within the realm; this morning, I have personally arrived at the palace of the Brahma King.
In the year Yichou of the Taiding era, Mount Jiangshan was struck by fire. One day, [the Emperor] asked the Master, "Since the temple has already been consumed by flames..."

The King asked, "Upon what does the Buddha rely for his dwelling? The Master replied, "The Buddhas of antiquity have passed away; the present Buddha has come again. He asked further, "How is the restoration proceeding?
The Master replied, "It relies upon the presence of a great donor. The King nodded his head. When he ascended [the throne],...
At the precious throne, he summoned the Master for an audience and granted him a seat. He again posed his previous questions and commanded the court historian Yu Ji and others to record them.
Regarding the verses from when Emperor Wen-tsung was still in the palace of his residence: having ascended Mount Zhong, he personally lifted a hoe to clear the mountain and establish [the monastery].
Emperor Xí commanded the Master to recite a verse. The Master respectfully responded with this verse:
The golden hoe has been raised three times, And the imperial foundation is vast. Ten billion mountains and rivers are viewed upon the palm;
For a thousand ages, Mount Zhongshan increases its auspicious aura, As the radiance of grace, like rain and dew, fills Longpan.
Congratulations on Donglin’s Chief Librarian Chengzang turning the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma; he has returned to his true station as one among the members of this community.
From the Peak of the Furnace, he leaps out through the eye of a lotus fiber, laughing the old, dull-witted Yanmen monk into a fit of laughter.
Xie Ping’s perilous cliffs bestow robes upon the myriad phenomena;
their essence is harmoniously integrated. Through ancient times, its merit of providing shelter has been difficult to measure. From where does this solitary, towering peak arise?
After the rain, at the clear dawn, it is sealed by white clouds.
Entrusted to my fellow practitioner in the city, Feng Songshan:

"All that exists is non-existence; all that is non-existent is fundamentally non-existent. This stone pillar at the crossroads preaches the Dharma with blazing intensity, delivering beings from the three miserable realms."
Seeing off a monk bound for Jiangxi:
On the river, green mountains rise in endless layers; beneath his feet, the official road stretches far away.
The colts have trampled down countless men, yet the ancestral wind of Shaoshi has not grown still.
Showing the Chan practitioner Xianguang:
Can you grasp the moonlight within the void? Before one’s eyes, the realm of conditions is free from confusion. The complete and perfect words of Caoxi and Shaoshi:
rain-washed autumn forests have many fallen leaves.

The bell-mound peak does not obey the command of Makara; lightning and sparks from flint have already traveled three thousand miles. With a single staff slung over his shoulder, he steps out the gate;
on another day, do not recklessly transmit this to all quarters.
Presented to Zhang Zhongde, Attendant of the Office of Ceremonial:

Your son has left the household life; it is fitting that you turn toward the good. Having no heart for official emolument, why not return to the plow? The myriad dharmas before one’s eyes are all empty and false;
Do not let idle sentiments defile your spiritual resolve.
Seeing off the Chan practitioner to Zhejiang—what joy fills my life!
How could it be otherwise? The mud ox bellows; the wooden man sings. Two, three, four, seven—there is no mysterious principle here.
From the hundred Yue and three Wu regions, the autumnal air abounds.
Presented to Zhao Yuxuan, Duke of Lugu: The Governor’s son, Qingyuan, is as clear and far-reaching as the sea;
The waves subside and the jade palace is vast. Who can behold the radiant breeze and the moon in its clarity? His father’s meritorious deeds transcend past and present;
At the head of the Nine-Bend Stream, ten thousand bamboo stalks stand tall.
Showing his disciple, Abbot Hui:
A three-legged donkey knows how to prance its hooves; through the ages, the monastic groves have witnessed this standard of conduct.
With a casual laugh atop Mount Zhong, eyebrows twelve inches long hang down from the chin.
Receiving the imperial decree, he entered the capital. While his boat was moored at Xuzhou, he composed a verse in the rhyme of Guangzhi:
Carrying my heavy golden staff once more, I enter the Imperial Capital; Boundless autumn colors assist my journey. Upon the banks of the Yellow River, the west wind blows fiercely;
At the fifth watch, the drum beats as the boat sets forth from its head.
Shi Congjing, the Prince who heads toward truth and treads in reality and emptiness; one who sees form with a clear mind and understands the matter. A broom-handle sprouts from the corner of a wall;
when the flowers bloom in profusion, it is yet the vernal season.
Chen, the Prefect, having received the Imperial Edict to craft the *naṃśī* dharma robes, spoke this verse as a gift:
"Do not merely measure others; you must measure yourself. Beneath the point of a single needle, a realm is established. This old monk does not move his ancient knife or ruler;
Throughout billions of worlds, the rain and dew are fragrant."
Presented to Zhao Andao, Grand Master for Correct Instruction, by Imperial Decree:
The brushwork that paints the Buddha image at Zhongshan surpasses the power of creation; Its sweeping and versatile mastery is transmitted through the mind.
A new beginning for Longpan Temple on Mount Zhongfu— May the grace of imperial favor endure for ten million years.
To Shiying Attendant:
Wandering abroad, you shall receive the seal of the blazing and unadorned; a poem of slight elegance from refined gold.
Where meaning and phrasing simultaneously fail to reach, the toes kick out the five Sumeru mountains.
Presented to the Layman Qīngzhēn:

Pure and clear, utterly free of stain, he has reached the state of true permanence. White lotus flowers bloom, their fragrance pervading the world. At his curved table and round rush mat, he passes the long days;
infinite wind and moon fill his hall and windows.
Sending Attendant Chuan back to Sichuan to visit his teacher:
The golden cock flaps its wings upon the jade balustrade; The void is shattered into fragments like a single lump of iron. He extends the ancient sage’s hand for rubbing one’s back;
In the Brocade River, there is no place for waves to stir.
Sent by Master Xin to the Capital:

The National Teacher called three times, and there was an immediate response three times. A single radiance of grace pervades every place; The central plains stretch ten thousand *li*, as level as the palm of a hand.
It would be well to take up the golden staff and wander the imperial streets.

A Letter Presented to Zen Practitioner Yue upon the Completion of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* Wandering through Zhejiang after finishing the *Huayan Jing*, I stand like a towering peak amidst surging waves. Fragrant waters float in the air from the tip of a single hair;
beyond a thousand peaks where the trees of the Chu sky have shed their leaves, tier upon tier of pavilions stand within the evening glow.
I present this seamless stupa for the Elder Earth-Immortal monk. It stands abruptly in a realm beyond yin and yang; north, south, east, and west all face it.
Within the crystal palace, the sun hall is empty.
Sending off Head Seat Huī back to his hometown:
The patched robe emerges from Dinglin amidst cold clouds; The autumn colors of ten thousand peaks strengthen the heart’s resolve to return. The Mahāyāna Dharma transcends words and speech;
It has swallowed and eclipsed all things since antiquity.
The Elder Song Tianzhi, having completed his term as Head Seat, returns to the Inner Court of Mount Cuifei to uphold the essential principles.

His mastery of the integration of illumination and function is like a miniature Śākyamuni. Amidst the autumn colors of the waters of Wu and the mountains of Yue, he dwells within the Dharma-king’s palace of a Buddha-field as vast as a mote of dust.
Shirun the guest prefect,
though this is but a matter of the gate and the threshold, his application belongs to one who transcends measure. With sinews in the eyes and blood in the skin,
a single bowl of spring tea immediately penetrates the divine.

To those who practice meditation and diligently cultivate precepts and samādhi, you, sons of the renunciant path, before the seven-foot single mat, the pivot of Buddhas and Patriarchs lies: thirty years of an iron-cast backbone;
thus, the waves of Deshan and Linji have subsided.
Sending off Venerable Huazang Xing, the rector:
With the golden mallet he strikes open the ocean of Huazang; amidst its waves, seventy-two peaks stand green. Alas, the young novice hastens his journey;
misty waters stretch boundlessly across a hundred or so cities.
Ziwei, Censor, travels north; I compose this "Snow Forest" to part with him as the year draws to a close.
I rejoice that you encounter the returning steed of the Censor, As auspicious light and auspicious mists fill the void. Upon the jade steps, a thousand trees are joined in silver blossoms;
May you offer the cup of ten-thousand-year longevity for a bountiful year.
Upon retiring from affairs at Mount Jiangshan, Master Xiyan offered me a congratulatory verse. I respond in the same rhyme:
The dragons and elephants of the Five Lakes have long ceased their inquiries; I, too, have never known how to point the way. My single staff is as fierce as a tiger;
For now, I follow my decrepit years and lie in the Eastern Hermitage.
A Poem of Congratulations by Master Xiaoyin, Appended to Lingyuan’s Retirement and Return to Zhaomo: "The lofty spirit of Jicui continues the tradition of Old Nan;
Today, the assembly of dragons and elephants at Mount Zhongshan— How can they bear to hear the drums beaten as he is sent back to his hermitage?"
I present to Master Shen this profound and vast great treasury: emptiness of nature is itself the lineage home of the Dharma King.
To search further through the vast expanse for the patriarch’s intent is like finding a flaw in flawless white jade.
Seeing off Attendant He Shanjun, while also [commemorating] Master Dongyuejiang: "How deep is the mountain stream?

Within it dwells a man of high attainment who serves as a patron for the Dharma. With a mere puff of cloth-hair, he rouses a power such that the mountains, rivers, and great earth have their very bones and pores chilled."
To send off Attendant Rui:
Bodhidharma never came to the Eastern Land, and the Second Patriarch likewise did not go to the Western Heaven. Nanyang three times called out, "Attendant!
For nearly a hundred years, tigers have galloped and dragons have surged forth.
The moon over Mount Zhong is clear as a jade dew-pool; the autumn wind off the Chu River is brisk with clouds. For the practitioner, going and staying are entirely without hindrance;
a single expanse of pure light is shared afar.
In the style of Master Lingshi, I compose this verse to see off the ninety-year-old Venerable Administrator Songwei of Tianning Monastery in Jiaxing as he sends his son away to travel:
How could the coiling dragons and crouching tigers ever repay him? High Peak has gone to weave his thatched hut;
how would the Buddhas and Patriarchs dare show their heads?
Entrusting this to Master Wuyan at Jiangxin:
"The moon beneath the water, four times seven and twenty-three; the old man upon the river—whom can he compare himself to? In my old age, I have devised a clumsy plan for this life:
three times I stirred the fire, only to seek out floating bubbles."
Xie Jing sends this letter from the midst of his mountain journey to the Record-keeper Ren, conveying the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* to Mount Jiangshan:
"The realms of infinite lands upon the tip of a single hair—every word is like a pearl rolling upon a jade platter. May the fifty-three [bodhisattvas] cease their slumber."
Letter. Master Longhua, do not deceive me.
You have honored me by showing me these wondrous verses; I have held and contemplated them without ceasing.
I have respectfully analyzed them into four stanzas and present this record at your feet to repay your great virtue. Submitted again by the Bhikṣu Zhiren, residing at Donglin on Mount Lu.

I prostrate at the tip of a single hair, where infinite lands and realms reside; the youth was deceived by the heat that year. On Mount Lu, as the winter month draws to a close, the plum buds are white;
on Mount Zhong, when the clouds have vanished, the moonlight is cold.

Every word is like a pearl rolling upon a jade platter; upon the golden palace, one beholds the Dragon’s countenance. The fragrance of the *dharma* flowers pervades the three thousandfold world-system;
he sits enthroned at the foremost mountain of Jiangnan.
Fifty-three people cease their sleepy chatter; though one might scoop up the great earth, not an inch of soil remains.
The resonance of metal and jade shatters the sand bowl; at midnight, the sun’s orb is high at noon.
Master Longhua, do not deceive us: the waves and billows of the ocean of teachings have been dried to their very bottom.
Three hundred pearls from within the curtain are clearly cast out for all to see.
The True Praise of the Buddhas and Patriarchs depicts the form of leaving the mountains:
the midnight star that changes one’s very eyes. Mahākāśyapa’s closed room—when the Dharma appears, the treacherous arise.
Potalaka the Bag-Carrying Monk keeps a single tattered bag. When was he born into this world? With his hands he plays with light and shadow; on the street, he terrifies small children.
Water-moon Avalokiteśvara.
The moon in the heavens and the moon in the water—sometimes dark, sometimes bright; sometimes full, sometimes incomplete.
Upon the White Flower Rock there has never been a word spoken; the pure vase and the willow tree alone are loquacious.
The Layman Vimalakīrti lay ill in Vaiśālī;
he was nearly becoming a stagnant commodity. When the Seven Buddhas, the Original Teacher, arrived, they all simultaneously took responsibility for him.
Looking around the chamber, how vast and empty it was! It could accommodate thirty-two thousand lion thrones.
In the *Mañjuśrī Asking after the Illness* painting, bystanders watch you two; whether speaking or remaining silent, both result in a lapse.
If no one knows of your illness, you shall sit alone in the city of Vaiśālī.
Venerable Zhaozhou— Zhaozhou of the world,
the most honored among the Dharma Kings, transcending the present and surpassing antiquity, swallowing and eclipsing heaven and earth.
East Gate, West Gate, South Gate, North Gate.
Master Yushan is worthy of laughter;
Old Chaling rides a donkey into the wild weeds. When he rises from one prostration, the thousand peaks are bright with the morning sun.
— Master Xugu.
Before the Hall of the Swastika, he cuts through all doubts with the decisiveness of a chisel; atop Mount Lingxiao, he strikes like lightning and thunders like a clap of thunder.
He brought down the imperial edict from the nine heavens and extinguished the true lamp of Vulture Peak. Such was the Chan Master Yuanjian, a monk peerless within the seas.
Master Huiji was a white-forehead tiger of Daxiong Peak, a tortoise-nosed snake of Nanshan. His compassion surpassed that of a Bodhisattva, and his wrath exceeded that of Nāṭa.
To say he was Buddha-wisdom is like pressing one's eyes and seeing flowers; to say he was not Buddha-wisdom is to willfully follow error. One thousand seven hundred [cases].
Following his lofty steps, he toppled the Lesser Śākyamuni of the Western Heaven.
Master Wawa occupied the summit of Mount Ou and the center of Mount Mufu; there he raised the clouds of Yunju and manifested the dragon of Huanglong. This is what is meant by that.
The Buddha-sun descends directly; there is no external Chan Master. He extinguishes the one school of Jibei.
Master Xiaoyin snaps in half the black lacquered bamboo whisk of Miaoxi, causing the monks to find him utterly distasteful. He shifts the constellations and alters the stars.
"Sun-face, Moon-face. Three times he received the imperial decree; his voice shook the ninefold heavens. He sat and cut off a thousand divergences, merely opening a single thread.
Master Yixi.
His conduct and realization were ethical and profound; the Son of Heaven praised him in high terms. For a thousand years, Baozhang had welcomed all with a smile.
His path atop the mountain peak was as brilliant as the sun and stars. When I spoke these words, the myriad phenomena listened intently.
Our late master, Venerable Yushan, had a pearl in his eye and no bone in his tongue.
He employed the "black bean" method of the patriarchs to test the monks of the world, wielding the Diamond King of Linji and manifesting the standard of the ancestral school.
At times, atop Dulong Peak, he presented an iron wall and a silver mountain.
Sometimes, amidst the silver mountains and iron walls of Vulture Peak, a stone woman suddenly conceives and gives birth to three parricides.
Tell me, who are they? They are Shouzong, Zhixian, and Liangbi.
Memorial for the Late Chan Master Gu on the Occasion of the Offering at the Three Pagodas:

In the third year of the Zhizhi era, the year of Guihai, on the second day of the tenth month, the news of the passing of my Dharma brother, the Great Monk Chan Master Gu, the Abbot of Jinge Chan Temple at the Three Pagodas in Jiaxing Prefecture, reached me from afar. [I,] the Abbot of Jiangshan Chan Temple...
The bhikṣu Shouchong, younger brother of Chihfa, respectfully presents this offering of pure delicacies and fragrant tea before the spirit-tablet, saying:
"Alas! The Way of our late Master was like Mount Tai or the Northern Dipper; all people looked up to it and gazed toward it.
Formerly when he resided at Lingquan, those who ascended his gate were beyond counting, yet those who were truly able to attain his Way..."
How rare! You alone have served as an attendant for a long time; your conduct has been upright and pure, and your realization is clear and penetrating.

Are you not truly one who has attained the Way of our late Master? In the past, when I served at Chongin Temple, although I was unable to fully practice the Way of the late Master, I remained cautious and diligent, never once becoming negligent.
At that time, you were staying in seclusion at Cold Spring (Lengquan), yet you did not shrink from the journey of a thousand li to come here from afar.

We visited one another. Amidst the blue lamps and night rain, we engaged in profound discussions regarding the Way of our late Master and the bond of brotherhood; these sentiments were as warm and harmonious as ever.
Subsequently, you, my elder brother, also responded to the summons of Jingde Temple. It was upon this that I privately relied on you;
for who else but you could have expanded the gate of our late Master and practiced his Way? Since I came to Beishan, I have been occupied day after day with responding to [official duties].
Because of my many obligations, I have been unable to correspond with you. Relying on your presence, I was certain that a time for our future meeting would surely come;

I never imagined that you would fall ill and that we would part forever in such a brief moment. From this day forward, who indeed shall be the one at the gate of Master Zhang who practices the Way of the Master?
If you have any awareness, you must surely know the sorrow of my words. This is the news of your passing.
I have come from afar; my intestines feel as if they have been cut. The mountains are empty and the moon is cold; cranes resent and monkeys are startled.
I draw the pure water to establish this sacrifice, and I summon my innermost feelings to offer these words. May the spirit not be oblivious; may it grant its response here.
In self-praise, the Head Seat Zushi requested the "Eye of Humanity and Heaven.
A solitary-horned auspicious qilin, he turns the seal of the Western Patriarch upside down; white days see angry thunder rushing, and tiles and pebbles [are transformed].
Within the courtyard stand jade towers and crystal palaces; amidst the vast ocean, earth is tossed and dust is raised.
Personally grasping a single unperforated flute, he blows forth the springtime of Shaolin upon the jade steps.
The disciple Maozong requests that the myriad streams flow toward the source and the thousand peaks reach the mountain. Alas, Master Sengyou! How can you depict this?
Beneath the pines of Beishan, before the time of Wei Yin—though father and son are close, the wondrous truth is not transmitted.
The Abbot Zhìyù invited [the Master] to sit upon the lion throne and wave his fly-whisk; the myriad phenomena listened to the Chan discourse, and even empty space joined in the exaltation.
As for Yangqi’s chestnut thorn and Dongshan’s secret code—do not be surprised that they do not coincide; though face-to-face, we are separated by a thousand li.
The lay practitioner Yang Yunyan requested:
"Is this real or unreal? Is it form or formless? It is like the great void of space, which contains all phenomena within it.
If you can recognize the true face of that person, you will not need to go beyond the chamber of Vimalakīrti.
At the request of Elder Jian of Chengdu’s Zhaojue Temple:
"The single, firm, and dense body is seen within every atom; where water is sprinkled, it does not adhere. On North Mountain, he walks with staff in hand."
When Shōin mixed mud with water, the twelve faces protruded from the crown of his head; he was a son who could uphold the family estate, whom [the Buddha] certainly did not wish to see.
At the request of the Elder Chōjō of Seizen-ji in Fuzhou.
Holding one hundred and eight prayer beads in his hand, the three poisons never arise within his breast.
At times he manifests a jade pavilion atop a heap of rubble; at times he blinds the eye at the crown of the monk’s head.
If anyone can discern where he lands, I grant you the power to manifest bodies throughout all dust-motes and lands.
The Elder Ming of Shangyan in Wuzhou requested:
"Within my breast there is a vast emptiness; beyond my body, the mind is at ease. I do not know what excellence I possess.
In the nine-layered city, he moves the Imperial Countenance.
The Abbot of the First Treasury was invited to grasp a black serpent while seated upon a lion throne; before he had even opened his mouth, he had already fallen into error.

The Buddhas of the three periods, the patriarchs of the six generations, and all the old monks of the world have become nothing but stale merchandise. At the spring dawn atop Wanfeng, the total upholding is revealed: a pure breeze sweeps across the earth.
Who else is there?
The Venerable Chief Administrator invites a three-legged donkey to prance on its hooves; it kicks out the primary truth of the noble path. Alas! Sengyou’s painting cannot capture it.
Accomplished! For a thousand ages, the monastic groves have held this as an auspicious omen.

When the Elder Yibei of Shengquan invited [him] to the three Buddha-halls, everything was beyond measure; he grasped "tortoise hair" upside down, causing both Buddhas and demons to perish. This is what is called "Duanfang."
This is clearly slander. To say it is not [the work of] Tanfang would, moreover, constitute a deception. "In this way, yet not in this way"—Buddha’s hand and a donkey’s hoof.
"Not in this way, yet in this way"—ash on the head, dust on the face. Once you blink your eyes, we shall meet again on another peak.

The Elder Guankui Yinqian is as high as ten thousand fathoms at Longmen; Guankui’s parting arrow is swift as lightning. He has thrown wide both gates of the double barrier and entered straight ahead with arms flung out.
The wooden horse neighs at Caoxi; the iron ox sleeps at Shaoshi. All at once, he entrusts this to the Elder Biefeng: "Blue-eyed one!"
Huangtou looked up but could not reach it. There is yet another move: a silver mountain and an iron wall.
Elder Chih of Dinglin requested [this]:
"The layout of the ancient temple at Dinglin reaches the heavens; a single stream flows across from the southeast. Without involving even a hair’s breadth, they meet."
Understood. A mistaken transmission between the human realm and the heavens.

At the request of the Elder Huaguang of Zushan, I have for my entire life carried a single shoulder-board. How does one restore the ancient? Seizing the dragon’s coil, the rain and dew are renewed; atop Mount Lingxiao, the sun shines.
At midday, he grasps tortoise hair upside down and brandishes a plain axe crosswise; casually releasing a tiger into the mountain grass, he nearly terrified the Patriarch of Shuangfeng to death.
The Moon Abiding in Illusion reflects in a thousand rivers; this is Master Fenzhou Zhongfeng painted here together with you in this same scroll.
I request a eulogy for him upon Dulonggang, within the Huanzhu Hermitage: his mirrored countenance is that of an ancient Buddha, he is the Illusionary Elder of Tianmu.
Like spring traveling through the myriad nations, like the moon shining across the sky; sometimes he sits alone atop Lion Rock, sometimes he sits firmly at the summit of Lingxiao Peak.
The method of using black beans has brought his fame to the four seas; smashing the sand bowl makes its sound shake the Nine Palaces.
Wherever there are waters in a thousand rivers, there is the moon; destroying the heterodox and manifesting the orthodox, he establishes the definitive principles of the school.
The Recorded Sayings of Venerable Master Tánfāng, Volume Lower (Concluded). Appended:
Eulogies on the Master’s Portrait by Contemporary Worthies.
By Zhào Shìyán, Duke of Lú and Minister of the Central Secretariat, courtesy name Zǐjìng.
The Sun rides upon the jade elephant, and the *udumbara* flower begins to bloom; the Dragon soars over the Abyss, and Mount Zhong grows in dignity.

At the height of one chi and five cun, wind and clouds meet; in ten lines of verse, rain and dew descend. This is indeed a rare encounter, none of which is not the result of having planted the roots of virtue in past lives.
As for seeking no trace within the Great Perfect Mirror, a single moon appears before a thousand rivers; the bamboo and trees of Dinglin Forest have long been like veteran practitioners.
His Majesty’s Imperial Academy of Literature (Hanlin), Grand Master for Receiving Edicts (Chengzhi) Zhang Qiyán, courtesy name Mengchén:

His mountain-like form is majestic and towering; his thunderous voice is vast and resonant. A *piān* and *nán* cedar among the groves of Chan, a dragon-elephant within the Dharma-gate—he continues the legacy of the two [masters] Bǎo and Fàn.
The ancestral lamp of a thousand years has manifested in the human realm with the physical appearance of a hundred-and-twenty-year-old. His mind was serene and his capacity was vast.
Though the fires of calamity fanned their cruelty, they could not disturb the sky of his nature. When the golden realm was renovated, it was entirely the product of his creative genius.
The king and his ministers took refuge [in him], and both the clergy and the laity looked up to him with reverence. How is it that such a majestic and imposing physique appears in this manner?
Is it because he is full yet does not overflow, or is it because humility is truly supreme?
Ouyang Xuan, Imperial Censor of the Hanlin Academy, courtesy name Yuangong:
When the Buddha, King of the Golden Wheel, appears in the world once, The fragrance of the *utpala* flower blooms for a single moment.
An old acquaintance within the Lion’s Seat has arrived; One who comes with ease upon the Phoenix Pond.

Scholar Lin Yujì, courtesy name Bóshēng, established his style amidst the coiling dragons and crouching tigers, manifesting the soaring phoenixes and perching pheasants. He sat before the Emperor in the Nine Palaces with his monk’s bowl and headcloth;
his physical form remained after a thousand years like the blade and ruler of a craftsman. Like the *utpala* flower, his fragrance pervades the earth; one seeks him as if following the water.
The moon reflects in the empty sky; ten-thousand-fathom Mount Kuanglu remains thus ever green.
Clouds rise from the northern mountains and rain falls on the southern peaks—once they protected the divine dragon as it emerged from the ancient pool.
For thirty years he sat in meditation at Daolin Temple, his wisdom perceiving the udumbara flower throughout the great trichiliocosm.
Dragons coil and tigers crouch; the green mountains are ancient. Amidst snow-covered bamboo and frost-hardened *jun* reeds, one sits in deep meditation.
If you wish to know the true face of this mountain, behold the *udumbara* flower blooming from the wondrously luminous mind.
Planting pine yields pine; sowing jade yields jade. The myriads-year-old lingzhi fungus and the ten-thousand-golden uncut gem arise and become human beings.
The lineage style is clearly manifest: unmoving and non-reliant, spiritual transformations appear before one, and the preaching of the Dharma is like clouds.

With the breeze of compassion and the sun of loving-kindness amidst the rivers and seas, he is fully endowed with the foremost [virtues]. I have heard that Bodhi dwells in the world for as long as a dragon;
it roars at the bottom of the sea while the phoenix dances in the celestial thoroughfare.
When An Manshuo was at the Hanlin Academy, he lived during the era of the Sage of the Central Kingdom.
Yet he practiced the teachings of the ancient sages of the West. When he remained in the mountains, the true dragon descended;
when he emerged from the mountains, the fierce tiger let out a long roar. Thus, he was able to respond to the convergence of wind and clouds—how could this be otherwise?
In sound and countenance, in speech and the half-mountain moon, for a thousand years you and the Master have illuminated one another.
Huang Jin, styled Jinjing, Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, bows his head:
When the *udumbara* flower appears, hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas culminate in this moment; as he discusses the profound mysteries with such loftiness, he transcends the present.
Ancient times. During the Tianli era, the Imperial Preceptor, Ke Jiusi (style name Jingzhong), Director of Calligraphy at the Quanzhang Pavilion, sat in silent meditation.
Greatly reviving the tradition of his school, within the state of samādhi and prajñā, he realized that the absolute void is not empty. There, the udumbara flower blooms.
Its fragrance is pure and refined; the flower follows the illusion of form, yet its scent never ceases. Thus, within this painting, it manifests this golden light.

Because it is devoid of self and others, even "non-existence" is forgotten. As for the power of his vows to establish great *caityas* while remaining free from attachment—how could this be the mere minor fruit of gods or humans?
To be graced by such favor and receive such extraordinary honors is like the waxing moon.
Amidst the clouds, there is nothing he cannot accomplish.
Inspector of the Censorate, whose name is Cha Ren (字: Shian), his blossoms are the udumbara;
he expounds the Dharma from the oceanic treasury. In the Tuṣita Heaven Palace, he was honored with a golden robe by the grace of the Former Emperor.

His life was one of command; with his jade whisk, he expounded the perfect penetration of the Great Being. The myriad phenomena of form and emptiness were illuminated by the brilliant luster of his singular pupils.
He was truly what is called a phoenix among men and a dragon among monks—a great spiritual friend (mahā-kalyāṇamitra).
The great dragon soars through the mountain;
the Milky Way flows across the heavens—neither boat nor oar can ferry one across. When the qilin and phoenixes roam the wilds, how could nets and snares ever bind them?
Therefore, one may take pride in the mountains and forests rather than the bronze tripods and bells; let the Way and its Virtue serve as one’s divining stalks and tortoise shell.

Since the conferred title is identical, he is none other than the master of the restoration at the time of Yuanwu. As the auspicious name perfectly fits, he is like the one called the National Teacher of Nanyang.
To the south of the Great River, on the slopes of Mount Zhong, the pavilions and towers of the Five Heavens surge forth; he molds ten thousand transformations within his forge, his merit—

Having achieved this, he does not dwell upon it; he relinquishes it as if casting it away. This solitary stride that transcends the clouds is truly due to the enduring regulations left by our ancestors.

It shall also move the hearts of the multitude of eminent monks, seeking the "horse's bones" from the Moon Cavern (*Yueku*) and gathering ten thousand *bhikṣus* like massed clouds, hoping for the transformation of the *kūrmara* (the great water-bird) within the heavens and earth.
Xingduan, the abbot of Mount Jing,
stands as a preeminent branch of the Ji North lineage and deepens the purity of the five streams of Songyuan. Having paid audience to the Son of Heaven atop the Golden Hall,
he emerges from the Phoenix City with his square-cut robes held high.

Wuxin, the mountain-dweller of Lingyin and the single lamp of Vulture Peak, is the fifth-generation descendant of the deaf old man [Zhaozhou]. His teachings and conduct spread throughout the land, resembling the golden age when the three Buddhas were at their zenith.

His Way harmonized with both gods and men; truly, this was a meeting of enlightened sovereigns and virtuous ministers for a thousand ages. In the space of a finger-snap, he manifested the Jewel-King Realm for this degenerate age.
He erected a great jeweled banner; for ten thousand ages, the monastic groves shall possess a brilliant light.
His dwelling on the mountain was as level as a grindstone—lofty and majestic, resplendent and glorious. A jewel among monks, a king of the Dharma, his voice resonated like jade and metal.

Continuing the lingering echoes of the six transmissions of the broken sand-basin, he withstood the ravages of frost and the cruelty of snow; he manifested the wondrous fragrance of the five-petaled *utpala* lotus.
It is said that Fahu once ascended the imperial dais, and Guangfozhao spent seven nights in the meditation hall.

Regarding fame, profit, and sustenance, he viewed them as soiled garments and refuse; taking loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity as his boat, raft, ferry, and bridge, his spirit swallowed ten thousand [miles].
The patched robe covers all quarters; praise cannot reach its excellence, and no depiction can truly capture it. Father and son do not transmit the true secret instructions;
atop the summit of Lingxiao Peak, a celestial fragrance is released.
King Aśoka dwelt upon the mountain with a seal of perfect correctness and vast compassion.
His wondrous, complete, and transcendent awakening caused the udumbara flower to bloom in fragrance; he opened the gate of nectar, his power of aspiration profound and far-reaching.
The Great Being Shijing (Real-Mirror) arrived, his virtue as lofty as the heavens.

Moved by the external protection of the Sage Ruler and worthy ministers, his fame surpassed that of the "National Teacher" (Guoyi). Seated grandly upon the peak of Mount Lingxiao, he presided over the hall;
holding a rank as eminent as the Duke of Nanyang, he watched the people’s boat races at the head of the Zhejin River. Secure and without peril, profound and firm, he composed [this work].
The main beam of the Great Dharma, the legitimate heir to celestial fragrance— this is what is called Mount Jing of the world,
the patriarch within the gate of the thousand monks.
Majestic as a soaring dragon, profound as a dragon’s abyss; the *udumbara* flower, its fragrance reaching to heaven.

With a single staff he entered the court to pay his respects, discoursing on the profound mysteries before the Emperor. Like cloud and dragon, wind and tiger, he opened a great dharma feast. The nature bestowed by Heaven, a flame continuing a fragrant lineage;
a auspicious presence in the world’s emerald heights, seated upon the Dharma King’s mat. He practiced the Way of the Teacher, wielding the authority of Buddhas and Patriarchs. [The Master] painted...
His appearance was majestic; his countenance was stern and imposing. He attained the rank of Duke of Nanyang and lived to the same age as Zhaozhou.
This eulogy for the śarīra relics is appended to the "True Seal of Mount Aśoka" by Ayuwang.
How great is his vast compassion! His wondrous perfection transcends awakening; merit and wisdom are both complete, and the fragrance of his Way spreads in all four directions.
His final stroke is brilliantly radiant—ashes fly and smoke vanishes, jade turns and pearls revolve. He is like Longqing Xian; he is like the venerable Zhenjing.
The śarīra were brilliantly radiant, their five colors crystalline and translucent. How magnificent was this Fragrance of Dharma (Tánfāng), who did not yield to the sages of antiquity!

Wherever the smoke reached, there were eighty-four thousand [relics]. A natural grandson of Heaven, an heir to Celestial Fragrance, he leaped over the hearth and pierced through the pavilion, surpassing the Buddhas and transcending the patriarchs.
A single nation of pure gold, north of the Tán and south of the Xiāng, enshrining the seamless stūpa—a *udumbara* flower for all eternity.
Qīngyù, abbot of Língyán on Píngjiāng Road, was thus:
he realized non-arising, possessed true wisdom, and attained nirvāṇa, causing the Dharma to flourish ever more brilliantly. At the time of his passing...

The *pi* incense was piled up; wherever the smoke reached, it formed *śarīra* relics, brilliant in five colors and of exquisite purity. Those who sought them obtained them, vying with one another in grief and joy.

Later arrivals could not contain their sorrow; they fell to the ground and leaped up, sobbing and sighing. They scraped away the ashes and mud, and suddenly [the relics] flowed forth and were sprinkled upon them.
Among the ancients, few were able to do so; when did the present age ever witness such a thing?
Alas, the Dharma-gate daily grows more withered, causing us followers to rely on this light of indignation to compose verses of praise to bequeath to our successors.
Postscript to the Five-Assembly Zen Records of the Great Chan Master Guangci Yuanwu. It is like a single drop of a lion’s milk that scatters ten *hu* of donkey’s milk;
it is also like a single drop of rain from the Dragon King that universally moistens the trichiliocosm. Therefore, it is said: [The weight of the Dharma].

The fame of this royal minister resounded throughout the world; as for those who could "pierce through the tower and leap over the hearth" like the venerable elder Tianxiang, there was only this master alone.
Even Linji and Deshan would have had to yield him ground by a head’s length before they could prevail.
